results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database. The mushroom body lobe system is further divided into a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages. VFB holds various data related to the mushroom body, including images, neurons with different types of connections to the mushroom body, parts and subclasses of the mushroom body, and tracts/nerves innervating it. For example, VFB has annotated [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body and [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") parts of the mushroom body.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila brain contains several types of Kenyon cells. VFB records show that there are [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), including [[KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain")(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open KCab-c(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCab-c, [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Kenyon cell of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open Kenyon cell of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, the connectome data indicates that these can be further categorized into main subtypes such as alpha/beta Kenyon cell, alpha'/beta' Kenyon cell, and adult gamma Kenyon cell, with subtypes including core, surface, posterior, anterior-posterior, middle, and dorsal. VFB holds 37 records of subclasses of Kenyon cell, as well as other relevant data, including images, scRNAseq data, transgene expression, downstream connectivity classes, and upstream connectivity classes for Kenyon cell. For more specific information, you can explore the available images of Kenyon cell, or examine the scRNAseq data, transgene expression, or connectivity classes for Kenyon cell.

results.title: Basic connectivity
results.question: What are the main input neurons to the mushroom body?
results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are sensory interneurons, as VFB records show the calyx, which is part of the mushroom body, receives sensory interneuron afferents. Additionally, VFB data indicates that projection neurons from the antennal lobe also provide input to the mushroom body. VFB holds [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") records of neurons with some part in the mushroom body, [366](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") records of neurons with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, and [304](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPostsynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with postsynaptic terminals in mushroom body") records of neurons with postsynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, which may be relevant for a narrower follow-up of mushroom body connectivity.

results.title: Circuit motif
results.question: Describe the dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs). Which DAN types connect to which MBON types?
results.response:
The dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) is provided by adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons. VFB holds extensive data on both MBONs and adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons, including their subclasses, transgene expression, and upstream and downstream connectivity classes. 

For MBONs, VFB has annotated [69](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of MBON") subclasses, as well as scRNAseq data and transgene expression in [158](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in MBON") records. The upstream connectivity classes for MBONs are recorded in [23,753](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for MBON") instances, and the downstream connectivity classes in [29,859](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for MBON") instances.

For adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons, VFB holds data on their subclasses, scRNAseq data, transgene expression, and both upstream and downstream connectivity classes, although the exact counts for these would require running the respective queries.

Regarding the specific connection between types of adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons (DANs) and MBONs, VFB does not currently hold specific data on which DAN types connect to which MBON types in the provided evidence. However, the available data on upstream and downstream connectivity classes for both MBONs and adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons could potentially be used to explore these connections further. 

The [larval mushroom body dopaminergic neuron h1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111634 "Open larval mushroom body dopaminergic neuron h1 in Virtual Fly Brain") is also represented in VFB with available data on its subclasses, transgene expression, and connectivity classes, but without more specific information, its connection to the dopaminergic input of MBONs cannot be determined from the available data. 

To determine the specific connections between DAN types and MBON types, further queries using the available VFB data or consulting additional sources would be necessary.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response:
The LPLC2 visual neuron type is known to have specific characteristics and functions. According to VFB, it is a type of Lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron with its cell body located in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind, as described by Wu et al., 2016. The LPLC2 neuron has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer, as reported by Klapoetke et al., 2017. This arrangement allows it to detect looming (expansion) stimuli. 

In terms of connectivity, VFB records show that in the lobula, the LPLC2 neuron has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4, as described by Wu et al., 2016, and Tanaka and Clark, 2022. Its arbors span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other LPLC2 cells, according to Wu et al., 2016. The LPLC2 neuron projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4, as reported by Wu et al., 2016.

The function of the LPLC2 neuron is related to eliciting a jump escape response, as described by Wu et al., 2016, and Klapoetke et al., 2017. VFB also records that there are approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe, as reported by Wu et al., 2016, and that they are cholinergic, according to Davis et al., 2020.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior. It has a large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum and a large descending axon that enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle. This information is based on data from VFB. 

VFB records show that the giant fiber neuron has specific anatomy and connectivity features. It has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons. It also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget. The axon enters the VNC near the dorsal midline and extends posteroventrally to the mesothoracic neuromere, where it turns ventrolaterally, and ends abruptly.

The connectome data indicates that the giant fiber neuron has downstream connectivity classes ([389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records) and upstream connectivity classes ([472](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records) available in VFB. 

VFB holds [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of the giant fiber neuron, [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNp01") splits targeting it, and [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in this neuron. 

Relevant publications include Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), Namiki et al. (2018), and Power (1948), which provide more information on the anatomy and function of the giant fiber neuron.

results.title: Concepts: NBLAST
results.question: What is NBLAST and what does an NBLAST similarity score mean?
results.response:
NBLAST is a method to quantify morphological similarity, as documented in the Virtual Fly Brain documentation. According to this documentation, NBLAST works by finding the closest tangent vector in the target neuron for each tangent vector in the query neuron and calculates a score from the distance between and the dot product of the two vectors. The final NBLAST score is the sum over all query-target vector pairs, typically normalized to a self-self comparison, with a perfect match being 1 after normalization, as described by Costa et al. (2016) and referenced in the Virtual Fly Brain documentation. 

VFB does not currently hold additional data on NBLAST beyond this documentation.
